newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock fund flows fell in 2-day period - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock fund flows fell in 2-day period - survey.

text.p: Flows into U.S. stock mutual funds fell to $46 million for the two-day period ended March 31 from $1.29 billion for the three-day period ended March 26, according to Mutual Fund Trim Tabs.

The fund tracking firm said aggressive growth funds suffered outflows of $185 million compared with inflows of $333 million, while growth fund inflows fell to $16 million from $204 million and growth and income fund inflows dropped to $215 million from $661 million. International fund flows fell to outflows of $71 million from inflows of $51 million.

Bond fund outflows narrowed to $23 million from $174 million. Muni fund outflows improved to $7 million from $248 million. Flexible/balanced/mixed funds inflows fell to $135 million from $272 million.
The data are based on about 50 fund firms that Trim Tabs follows.
Trim Tabs estimated that overall industry inflows for the two days was $838 million compared with $2.7 billion for the three-day period.

Industrywide, it estimated that aggressive growth funds suffered outflows of $113 million versus inflows of $659 million, while growth and income funds had inflows of $540 million versus $1.2 billion, and growth funds inflows slowed to $237 million from $517 million.
Overall, bond funds had inflows of $94 million versus outflows of $191 million, it said.
